answer: No. The older notarized form, NW-POA-1, was replaced by NW-POA-2 on February 1, 2026, and an NW-POA-1 signed before that date is only accepted until June 30, 2026, so it won't be valid for your July 10 appointment. Your mom can sign the newer form NW-POA-2 instead, which can be signed electronically with no notary. If you're in Georgia, the power of attorney, including NW-POA-2, must still be notarized.
